visual.title: Your architecture lives in a hundred places
visual.subtitle: spreadsheets · diagrams · slide decks · people's heads

scenes.narration: Ask five people how your systems fit together and you get five spreadsheets, three diagrams and a slide deck from last year. None of them agree, and none of them are current.

captions.text: Ask five people how your systems fit together and you get five spreadsheets, three diagrams and a slide deck from last year.

scenes.narration: Atrium gives your organisation one living map. Capabilities, applications, data and technology, and how they connect. Architects keep it right. Managers use it to decide. Engineers, and their AI coding assistants, build with it.

captions.text: Atrium gives your organisation one living map.

scenes.narration: You already know your landscape. It's just spread over spreadsheets, wikis and diagrams that went stale the day they were drawn. Here is how Atrium turns that into one model you can trust, in an afternoon.

scenes.narration: Start with what you have. Drop in an export from your CMDB, an Excel list or an ArchiMate file. Atrium works out what each column means, matches rows to what is already there so nothing is duplicated, and shows exactly what will change before you click Import. Next time, it remembers the layout.

scenes.narration: Fields that can be worked out are filled in for you: versions and end-of-life dates for technology, owners and domains inherited from their parents, and likely links between applications and capabilities. Suggestions stay grey until you accept them, one at a time or all at once.

scenes.narration: Now the picture. The capability map shows which applications support what, coloured by health, cost, lifecycle or fit. Click any box and the inspector opens beside it, so you can edit in place without losing your view.

visual.title: Decisions in three clicks
visual.subtitle: for managers with a technical background

scenes.narration: You need straight answers. What do we run, what does it cost, where is the risk, and are we moving in the right direction? Atrium puts those answers one click from the landing page.

captions.text: You need straight answers.
What do we run, what does it cost, where is the risk, and are we moving in the right direction?
Atrium puts those answers one click from the landing page.

scenes.narration: The portfolio dashboard shows how healthy your applications are, where the money goes per domain, and which systems to invest in, tolerate, migrate or eliminate. Health is worked out from fit ratings and technology lifecycles, so it stays current without anyone updating a slide.

captions.text: The portfolio dashboard shows how healthy your applications are, where the money goes per domain, and which systems to invest in, tolerate, migrate or eliminate.
Health is worked out from fit ratings and technology lifecycles, so it stays current without anyone updating a slide.

scenes.narration: Every number is a door. Click the share that needs action and you see the applications behind it, with the reasons: unsupported technology, poor fit, or a platform being phased out.

captions.text: Every number is a door.
Click the share that needs action and you see the applications behind it, with the reasons: unsupported technology, poor fit, or a platform being phased out.

scenes.narration: Cost per capability shows what the business actually pays for each thing it does, not just per system. It is the fastest way to spot duplication: three applications doing the same job.

captions.text: Cost per capability shows what the business actually pays for each thing it does, not just per system.
It is the fastest way to spot duplication: three applications doing the same job.

scenes.narration: End-of-life exposure lists the technologies that are out of support, or soon will be, and which applications rely on them. That is your risk register, built from facts.

captions.text: End-of-life exposure lists the technologies that are out of support, or soon will be, and which applications rely on them.

scenes.narration: The roadmap shows initiatives and system lifecycles on one timeline. Ask a question in plain words, such as what breaks if we retire the legacy CRM, and get the answer straight away.

scenes.narration: Architecture documentation usually lives far from the code, so it goes stale. Atrium meets you where you work: in your repository, your pipeline and your terminal.

captions.text: Architecture documentation usually lives far from the code, so it goes stale.

scenes.narration: Your home page shows your team's services, their health, and what needs attention: an end-of-life runtime, a missing owner, a suggestion waiting for you. Services your team owns, you can edit directly.

captions.text: Your home page shows your team's services, their health, and what needs attention: an end-of-life runtime, a missing owner, a suggestion waiting for you.

scenes.narration: Each repository can describe itself in a small atrium.yaml file. You don't write it from scratch: one command, atrium init, reads your package files, Dockerfile and compose files and fills in the runtime, frameworks, databases and dependencies.

captions.text: Each repository can describe itself in a small atrium.yaml file.

scenes.narration: Atrium check compares that against your organisation's standards and technology radar, and against end-of-life dates. It fails the build only for real problems, and explains each one in plain words.

captions.text: Atrium check compares that against your organisation's standards and technology radar, and against end-of-life dates.

scenes.narration: In your pipeline, atrium sync keeps the model in step with the code. Changes to services your team owns are applied straight away. Anything else becomes a suggestion for an architect.

scenes.narration: Atrium context writes an ARCHITECTURE.md for your service: what it supports, what it depends on, who uses it, and the standards that apply. It is always generated from the live model, so it is never out of date.

captions.text: Atrium context writes an ARCHITECTURE.md for your service: what it supports, what it depends on, who uses it, and the standards that apply.
It is always generated from the live model, so it is never out of date.

captions.text: Everything you see is also available through a documented REST API, and webhooks tell your other tools the moment something changes.

scenes.narration: Describe your service once, let the pipeline keep it current, and get guidance before you merge. Less documentation work, better documentation.

captions.text: Describe your service once, let the pipeline keep it current, and get guidance before you merge.

scenes.narration: This is built to be safe. Each connection has its own token that you can revoke at any time. It only sees information up to the level you choose, enforced twice, including by the database itself. Agents can only suggest, never change. Everything they return is marked as data, not instructions, and every request is logged.
